name: Zahmer Kaiser & Kaisertal
kurzbeschreibung: Zahmer Kaiser entices with gentler forested ridges, the serene Kaisertal valley, Vorderkaiserfeldenhütte, and vistas over Kufsteinerland.
preis: Mountain trails freely accessible; Zahmer Kaiser chairlift in Durchholzen chargeable
oeffnungszeiten: Freely accessible year-round; alpine huts serviced from May to late October
beschreibung:
Overview

The majestic mountain range of the Zahmer Kaiser forms the northern, heavily forested and meadow-draped crest of the celebrated Kaisergebirge in the Tyrolean lowlands. In charming contrast to the forbidding limestone spires of the neighboring Wilder Kaiser to the south, the Zahmer Kaiser welcomes hikers with gentler ridges, fragrant mountain forests, and rolling high pastures. Its highest point is the 2,002-meter Vordere Kesselschneid, closely followed by the striking Pyramidenspitze at 1,997 meters. Nestled between the Inn Valley, Lake Walchsee, and the car-free Kaisertal – voted Austria's most picturesque place in 2015 –, this protected nature reserve captivates with serene alpine tranquility, diverse orchid meadows, and historic pastoral landscapes that shine in brilliant colors especially in early summer and autumn.

Route & Requirements

The trail network of the Zahmer Kaiser caters to hikers of all experience levels. A classic route starts in Ebbs, climbing the historic Kaiserstiege steps into the car-free Kaisertal and across flowering meadows up to the celebrated Vorderkaiserfeldenhütte at 1,388 meters (approx. 2.5 hours, 880 vertical meters, moderate T2). The hut is celebrated for its unmatched panoramic view across the vertical north walls of the Wilder Kaiser. From the hut, ambitious hikers continue to the summit of Pyramidenspitze (approx. 2 hours, surefootedness on rocky paths required). Families frequently take the 4-seater Zahmer Kaiser chairlift in Durchholzen near Walchsee for leisurely pasture strolls. Ankle-high hiking boots with reliable grip and ample drinking water are necessary on sun-exposed paths.

Visit & Arrival

Trailheads are located in Kufstein, Ebbs, and Walchsee. Motorists travel toll-free via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Kufstein-Nord) directly to Ebbs. Ample paid hiker parking is provided at the Kaisertal trailhead in Ebbs-Kaisertal. By public transit, take trains to Kufstein station and connect via regional buses (lines 4030 or 4036) directly to the Kaisertal entrance.

Tips

Linger at Vorderkaiserfeldenhütte to enjoy freshly prepared Kaiserschmarrn on the outdoor terrace while sunset paints the vertical cliffs of the Wilder Kaiser in glowing alpine light. Bring binoculars to scan the rocky ledges for chamois and golden eagles, and discover more than thirty rare mountain flowers in the historic alpine garden beside the hut.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Kaisertal-Hauptweg auch im Winter geräumt)
